opener: One list, one inn's name. Nothing was taken.
questionTitle: Were you meant to have the list?
forkA: He was sent to put it in your hands.
forkB: You took it off a man carrying it somewhere else.
nudge: A man who takes nothing, and leaves a list. Who would want you to have it?

fanOutClue.title: The even hand
fanOutClue.text: Not one name is crossed out or written over. Every line sits level, and the inn's line is in the same hand as the names.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

opener: You've paid for your rooms and you haven't burned anything down. That's more than most guests manage.
questionTitle: The child in Meira's notes: when was that child taken?
forkA: Lately. Whatever was happening there is happening now.
forkB: Long ago. She was writing about an older taking.
callback: She hasn't sat in that seat for three weeks. Your pages all reached you on the road within the same few days.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, the page about the child has no date. What would give it one?

nudgeIfLaid.line: {friend:Intellect}, that leaf. What does it tell you about when she wrote it?

puzzle.q: Did Meira leave in a hurry?
puzzle.clickText: Every slip still sits where she pinned it, and the page about the child is the one her thumb wore soft. A woman packing in fear does not leave her book in order. She did not go in a hurry.

clicks.text: Every slip still sits where she pinned it, and the page about the child is the one her thumb wore soft. A woman packing in fear does not leave her book in order. She did not go in a hurry.

fanOutClue.title: Read the stubs
fanOutClue.text: Each stub has a faint straight line scored down it. She cut them against a rule, one at a time, with care. She meant to send them.

opener: You've not eaten. Sit.
questionTitle: When he ran for the smoke, was he running home?
forkA: Fenmark is his.
forkB: Fenmark is on his way.
callback: The man on the forest road was carrying her rubbing. The man in the bracken was watching her rock.
nudge: {friend:Agility}, he ran toward the smoke. What lies that way for a man like him?

puzzle.q: How long has this rock been watched?
puzzle.clickText: Someone has sat over this rock for hours at a time, and walked round it often enough to wear the turf away. It is watched, and it has been for a long while.

clicks.text: Someone has sat over this rock for hours at a time, and walked round it often enough to wear the turf away. It is watched, and it has been for a long while.

fanOutClue.title: The second ring
fanOutClue.text: In the flattened bracken a flask has left a ring in the dew, and a second ring beside it where he set it down again.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

narratedSilence: Garrick sets a bowl in front of each of you, and for once he says nothing at all.
questionTitle: Why did they take Tamsin, of all the children in Fenmark?
forkA: She was someone in particular. They came for her.
forkB: She was the easiest to take.
callback: The boy says they moved like they'd done it before. The little horse at the rock had sat out a winter or two.
nudge: {friend:Charm}, of all the children in Fenmark, why her?

nudgeIfLaid.line: {friend:Charm}, three doors, with children behind them. Why hers?

fanOutClue.title: The leaned bar
fanOutClue.text: The gate at the end of the lane is swinging, but its bar has been lifted and leaned neatly against the post, not thrown down.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

opener: Two winters between two children. Some people count in winters. It's a way of keeping still.
questionTitle: Is it the same man, twice, or a way of working?
forkA: It's the same man, twice.
forkB: It's a way of working, not one man.
callback: The road, the rock, and tonight her shutters. Not one of those men has said a word.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, she knows him by a knife, and the knife in that camp is a kitchen blade. Which do you trust?

puzzle.q: Has someone tried her house before tonight?
puzzle.clickText: The marks on her back shutter are old and new in the same place, and the bar on her door has worn its cleats deep. Someone has tried her house before tonight, and she has barred it every night for a long time.

clicks.text: The marks on her back shutter are old and new in the same place, and the bar on her door has worn its cleats deep. Someone has tried her house before tonight, and she has barred it every night for a long time.

fanOutClue.title: The knife, not the face
fanOutClue.text: She says she never saw his face, only the knife, and it is the knife she knows him by.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Rewritten 10 Oct after the check against the chapter text.

opener: Six pieces, one map. Eat something before you stare at it.
questionTitle: Why are our names on that list?
forkA: We are like the children. They want us too.
forkB: Meira chose us, to help her find them.
callback: Meira had this shape on paper before any of you found a piece. Tonight the pieces drew it.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, that list has been in your pocket all week. Tell the table what you make of it now.

puzzle.q: Why send the cart one way and the child another?
puzzle.clickText: One man carried her down to the water, the other went back up to the cart, and the cart went up the far bank at a run, without her. Anyone who followed the cart was following an empty one.

clicks.text: One man carried her down to the water, the other went back up to the cart, and the cart went up the far bank at a run, without her. Anyone who followed the cart was following an empty one.

fanOutClue.title: Wade out
fanOutClue.text: Mid-stream, on the upstream side of the ford-stone, a scrape of fresh paint on the rock at the height of a gunwale. There was a boat.
fanOutClue.qaNote: Existing [PRESS ON] detail. Leans 'carried her across'.

place: The mine, then the mill road
opener: Beds are in the barn tonight. Pick a corner and take it.
questionTitle: The cart passed three sleeping farms in the dark and stopped only at the mill. Why?
forkA: Someone was waiting on the road to guide them in.
forkB: They had one destination before they ever entered the valley.
callback: The mine wall put Tamsin's name first and Corin's second. Tamsin heard them say "the mill boy next".
nudge: {friend:Aim}, an old man with two winters of firewood split behind him, watching one road. What was he waiting for?

puzzle.q: How did the cart travel in the dark?
puzzle.clickText: The horse never checked at the fork on the way up, and coming down the wheels sank deep into the verge. The cart went up empty and came down laden.

clicks.text: The horse never checked at the fork on the way up, and coming down the wheels sank deep into the verge. The cart went up empty and came down laden.

fanOutClue.title: The steady horse
fanOutClue.text: The old man says the horse never balked at his gate or at the fork, in full dark and with no lamp. It took the mill lane at a steady walk.

opener: Asked for by name, and by the night he was born. That's a strange thing to ask for.
questionTitle: How did a stranger know the night the boy was born?
forkA: From an old record kept somewhere far from here.
forkB: Someone from this valley told him.
callback: In the mine, that shape was a hole, and what sat in it was gone. Here it's cut into the mill's footing.
nudge: {friend:Craft}, look at that footing stone again. The wheel is fifty years old, but the mark under it is older than the valley. How long has that mark been waiting?

puzzle.q: Did he hesitate once he reached the house?
puzzle.clickText: The mud on the floorboards runs in one unbroken line from the door to the child's bed, and the paper was in his fist before he crossed the threshold. He did not search the house.

clicks.text: The mud on the floorboards runs in one unbroken line from the door to the child's bed, and the paper was in his fist before he crossed the threshold. He did not search the house.

fanOutClue.title: The ruts
fanOutClue.text: The left wheel pulls. You have seen that track before, coming down a muddy bank to a ford. It is the same cart.

opener: A stranger dead at a lock, and the lock opens for you. Stone doesn't have favourites without a reason.
questionTitle: The dead man picked at the housing for days. Why did it give under your bare hand?
forkA: The stone woke to the fragments in our pack.
forkB: The stone woke to the hand that touched it.
callback: Corin was asked for by name. Today a lock that wouldn't open for a dead man opened for you.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, a dog chained between two rocks four nights ago, fed fresh meat, and a dead man left on the path. Who is keeping that road?

puzzle.q: Why didn't anyone rob him?
puzzle.clickText: He worked that stone for days with steel, and his belt is still weighted with coin. The path-keeper stepped over his body for a week and took neither his tools nor his purse.

clicks.text: He worked that stone for days with steel, and his belt is still weighted with coin. The path-keeper stepped over his body for a week and took neither his tools nor his purse.

fanOutClue.title: The scratches
fanOutClue.text: The stone round the housing is scored with dozens of short scratches, some weathered and some bright. He tried it more than once, on more than one day.

opener: Sit down. Keep your voices under the wind.
questionTitle: They pulled the ladder, but they didn't run. Why didn't they scatter when we were spotted?
forkA: They have too many guards down there to fear a handful of strangers.
forkB: Whatever they are doing to the boy cannot be paused for anything.
callback: Yesterday a branch swung on the slope with no wind. Today they knew you were at the shaft.
nudge: {friend:Charm}, you saw his hands before they hauled the ladder up. Not a scratch on him yet. What are they waiting for?

fanOutClue.title: The second lamp
fanOutClue.text: A second lamp stands lit at the foot of the shaft, filled and trimmed, the same make as the ring in the chamber. Nobody grabbed it in a hurry.

opener: A circle of black cloth, and a man who fought without a word. Somebody wanted a name forgotten.
questionTitle: Meira found every record of him scraped clean. Who erased his name from the world?
forkA: His enemies tore his name down to break those who followed him.
forkB: His own people hid his name to keep what he did a secret.
callback: At the mill a horn button, on the river path a dead stranger. Tonight, a circle.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, a scout who fights without a sound, tears his own coat to get free, and flashes a lamp twice toward the dark. Who teaches a man to fight like that?

puzzle.q: Were the stones broken or hidden?
puzzle.clickText: The carved monuments on the ridge were shattered with fire and mallet, but the cut stones in the sheepfold were laid face-inward against each other. Some were broken in anger, and some were hidden with care.

clicks.text: The carved monuments on the ridge were shattered with fire and mallet, but the cut stones in the sheepfold were laid face-inward against each other. Some were broken in anger, and some were hidden with care.

fanOutClue.title: The ground-flat face
fanOutClue.text: On the old stone where the scout stood, one face has been ground flat, long ago. The chisel scars are weathered grey. Whatever was carved there is gone.

opener: Picks in the deep rock. They're digging toward something that was here before them.
questionTitle: The fragments drew a map to an older room. Why are they digging toward that same room tonight?
forkA: They know what is inside that room, and came to take it.
forkB: They are digging toward the boy, and do not know the old room exists.
callback: In the mine, you reached the mark after it was emptied. Tonight they're still digging toward the older room.
nudge: {friend:Might}, feel that vibration through the turf. Those picks haven't rested once since twilight. How many men are down there swinging iron?

puzzle.q: What are the picks searching for?
puzzle.clickText: The pick-strokes fall in one unbroken line toward the deeper stone, and every basket of earth is sifted through bare fingers. They are not clearing rock for a tunnel. They are searching for something small.

clicks.text: The pick-strokes fall in one unbroken line toward the deeper stone, and every basket of earth is sifted through bare fingers. They are not clearing rock for a tunnel. They are searching for something small.

fanOutClue.title: Ear to the rock
fanOutClue.text: Under the room with the lamps there is another hollow. It is bigger. And there is nobody in it at all.

opener: Somewhere warm. I'd settle for a warm supper. Eat.
questionTitle: Corin said they promised Wren she was going home first. Why tell a stolen child that?
forkA: A lie to keep a child quiet and docile on the road.
forkB: The truth: her home in the burned country is where their work needed her.
callback: Corin was held a morning's walk from his own mill. Wren was told she was going home first.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, a child's mitten tucked in Corin's belt, smelling of sheep. Who gives a mitten to another child in the dark?

puzzle.q: Did the cart make ready for a long journey?
puzzle.clickText: The cart below the shaft took the west road without checking, and on the ridge above the runner paused only to watch that same line. They did not search for a trail. They set their faces toward the burned hills and walked.

clicks.text: The cart below the shaft took the west road without checking, and on the ridge above the runner paused only to watch that same line. They did not search for a trail. They set their faces toward the burned hills and walked.

fanOutClue.title: The grey wool
fanOutClue.text: Corin has a child's woollen mitten tucked in his belt that is not his. The wool is rough and grey, and it smells of sheep.

narratedSilence: Garrick sits by the hearth with his boots off, watching the embers in silence.
questionTitle: The men in grey coats spoke politely and promised she'd only be needed once. Was that courtesy genuine?
forkA: Yes: they take what the rite requires, and let the children go.
forkB: No: a polite kidnapper is only a kidnapper who hates a scene.
callback: Tamsin and Corin each came home with one cut palm, bound clean. Wren's taker said they'd only need her the once.
nudge: {friend:Charm}, chips of black glass set in a row on her windowsill, dusted around with care. Why leave them behind?

fanOutClue.title: The boy at the well
fanOutClue.text: At the well a boy holds his chip out low and quick, then shoves it back into his shirt before you have looked at it properly.

opener: Sit, before that glass has the rest of your boots, and mind your hands on it.
questionTitle: Three children live beside three Seeker marks. Why did the riders carry Wren straight past the Blackglass?
forkA: They cannot open these ancient housings; they need an older entrance.
forkB: The marks are not their goal; they are only the guide-stones to the place they are making for.
callback: At the Widow's Tooth a man lay in the bracken watching the rock. Here the riders went past this one without slowing.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, Meira's note in the margin: 'Five, the fragment says. Every other record says four.' Why would a scholar write down a number she doubted?

puzzle.q: Has anyone touched this housing since the road was made?
puzzle.clickText: The old shepherds' path ends dead at the sunken stones, and the fine dust over the housing was undisturbed until your fingers reached it. The riders stayed on the crest and rode past without once looking down.

clicks.text: The old shepherds' path ends dead at the sunken stones, and the fine dust over the housing was undisturbed until your fingers reached it. The riders stayed on the crest and rode past without once looking down.

fanOutClue.title: Read the scratches
fanOutClue.text: Six horses. One of them is carrying double, and the second rider weighs almost nothing.

opener: Whoever slept in these niches had long nights too. Build the fire in the doorway.
questionTitle: Wren is dropping glass chips from the saddle of six horses. Have the riders truly not noticed?
forkA: They believe a small child is helpless and don't watch her hands.
forkB: They see the chips, but know the trail ends where no one can follow.
callback: Tamsin wasn't asleep; she was counting. Wren is dropping her chips, one by one, on their trail.
nudge: {friend:Craft}, a bone die with its spots worn smooth, left in a sleeping niche centuries ago. What kind of soldiers played with that?

puzzle.q: Did she drop the chips in haste or with care?
puzzle.clickText: Each chip was set on high bare rock where the starlight catches it, and the backs are scored with tiny knife-scratches: one, two, three. She is laying a numbered line across the dark.

clicks.text: Each chip was set on high bare rock where the starlight catches it, and the backs are scored with tiny knife-scratches: one, two, three. She is laying a numbered line across the dark.

fanOutClue.title: Scratched on the back
fanOutClue.text: Turn the chips over. One has a single short scratch on its back, one has two, and one has three.

opener: They ran this time, and left their supper on the fire. Sit down and get your breath. They'll be needing theirs.
questionTitle: They gave Wren the warm bed by the hearth, yet left at a run this morning, with the pot still on the fire. What made them run?
forkA: Fear: our fire on the ridge showed them they were being hunted.
forkB: The hour: their waiting was over, and wherever they are taking her, it had to be now.
callback: At the mine someone took the time to bind Tamsin's hand in clean linen. Here someone folded one blanket with care, and threw the other down.
nudge: {friend:Might}, cut deep into the beam over her bed: 'Until the throne rise whole.' Who carves a prayer over a stolen child's pillow?

puzzle.q: How quickly did they depart?
puzzle.clickText: By the spring a water skin lies half full where it was dropped; inside, by the pallet, one keepsake is gone from its row, and the dust where it lay is clean. She had time to take one thing. The hurry began outside.

clicks.text: By the spring a water skin lies half full where it was dropped; inside, by the pallet, one keepsake is gone from its row, and the dust where it lay is clean. She had time to take one thing. The hurry began outside.

fanOutClue.title: Cut twice
fanOutClue.text: Each stroke of the name has been cut twice, the second pass deeper than the first.

opener: Fire's built up. Sit by it before you decide anything.
questionTitle: An hour after we read the map into the wind, a single lamp climbed the Kiln and went inside. Who carried it?
forkA: A watcher who heard our voices and went in to warn the others.
forkB: The last of the faithful arriving for the ritual, unaware of us.
callback: Corin said Wren's home was always warm. Tonight the map ends at a hill that breathes warm air.
nudge: {friend:Agility}, the knife-edge drops straight to scree on both sides. If we go down in the dark, how do we keep from sliding?

puzzle.q: Are the riders still inside the hill?
puzzle.clickText: No horses wait outside in the dark, and from the crown's crack thin pale smoke has begun to rise into the cold air. The lamp has reached the deep chamber, and the hearth is burning.

clicks.text: No horses wait outside in the dark, and from the crown's crack thin pale smoke has begun to rise into the cold air. The lamp has reached the deep chamber, and the hearth is burning.

fanOutClue.title: No horses
fanOutClue.text: Not one horse is tethered at the foot of the Kiln, though six rode this way.

opener: Count yourselves. I will, too.
questionTitle: Someone stood among us in the dark with a bare blade, yet cut only rope. Why spare us?
forkA: A lone rescuer couldn't risk a fight in the dark without losing the prisoner.
forkB: They had us at their mercy and were under orders not to harm us.
callback: Every one of them you've fought has run at the first gap. Tonight one stood among you with a blade and cut only rope.
nudge: {friend:Craft}, cut rope ends all clean on the same side, a finger's width from the knot. Someone stepped out of that passage with a steady blade.

puzzle.q: How did the prisoner get free in the dark?
puzzle.clickText: A lamp was just snuffed inside the side passage, and every rope was severed cleanly on the same side a finger's width from the knot. A second person stepped out of the passage in the dark and cut him loose.

clicks.text: A lamp was just snuffed inside the side passage, and every rope was severed cleanly on the same side a finger's width from the knot. A second person stepped out of the passage in the dark and cut him loose.

fanOutClue.title: Follow them
fanOutClue.text: They end where the ash gives out and the rock turns to bare black glass. No prints come in. Whoever cut him loose came over the glass and was waiting.

opener: Cold road. Hands round that cup first, and get the warmth back into them. The rest will keep.
questionTitle: Four armed riders guarded one small box from the Kiln, riding away from the lake. Why guard that box harder than the boy?
forkA: The box holds what they actually came for; the child only wakes it.
forkB: The cart was an open-road decoy meant to draw our eyes off the lake.
callback: The carter's coin has the king's face scraped off. Meira wrote that every record of him had been scraped clean.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, bare swords across their saddles and eyes never leaving a single small box in the cart-bed. Why ride like that in broad daylight?

puzzle.q: How did the four riders guard the cart through the settlements?
puzzle.clickText: They rode with bare blades across their saddles in broad daylight, never speaking and never once looking at the road or the lake. Every eye stayed locked on the single small box in the cart-bed.

clicks.text: They rode with bare blades across their saddles in broad daylight, never speaking and never once looking at the road or the lake. Every eye stayed locked on the single small box in the cart-bed.

fanOutClue.title: Every eye on the cart
fanOutClue.text: The carter says the four never spoke to each other, and never once looked at the road or the lake. Every eye stayed on the cart.

narratedSilence: Garrick sits by the window looking out over the water, his arms folded in the quiet room.
questionTitle: They took Joss eight nights ago — before we even reached the Kiln — and have kept him on the water ever since. What are they waiting for?
forkA: A night or a water-level that hasn't come yet to reach the drowned chamber.
forkB: Someone else who had not reached Reedham yet: they have been waiting for us.
callback: In Ashcombe a baby born when the moon goes out is given a chip of black glass. In Reedham every window is lit for one.
nudge: {friend:Craft}, eight notches cut in her doorpost wood, and a boat heavier than her skiff touching the shingle by night.

fanOutClue.title: The oars at dusk
fanOutClue.text: On the shingle the fisherman says he hears oars out on the lake every night, at the same hour, just after dusk. He has never gone to look.

opener: Drowned streets, and a page of Meira's with one line scratched out. Let's hear what you found.
questionTitle: Meira's note says 'moon-blood' is the old word for the marked, and the fragment warns against letting it near. What is the fragment warning against?
forkA: Letting a marked child's blood touch the stones in the housings — the Order is doing what the Seekers feared.
forkB: Letting a specific bloodline from the old songs near — 'moon-blood' may mean more than the birth-mark.
callback: At the ford, Tamsin's small prints stopped at the water. Today Joss's stop at the edge of deep water.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, she copied 'the marked' on one page and 'moon-blood' on another, then crossed out her second line in the margin until the nib tore through.

puzzle.q: Was Meira sure of her own note on 'moon-blood'?
puzzle.clickText: Meira copied 'the marked' and 'moon-blood' from two separate old records, and under her gloss she began a second thought before scratching it out through the paper. She had a second thought she never finished.

clicks.text: Meira copied 'the marked' and 'moon-blood' from two separate old records, and under her gloss she began a second thought before scratching it out through the paper. She had a second thought she never finished.

fanOutClue.title: The small prints
fanOutClue.text: In one place the small prints stop and turn with both heels dug in: from that exact spot, you can see his grandmother's window on the shore with its lamp burning.

opener: Pale curls of whittled wood. Somebody's still carving.
questionTitle: They ferry Joss between the island and the drowned streets by night, yet tonight a lamp is crossing to the empty tower. Why the tower tonight?
forkA: They shift their watch-post across the lake so no one on shore can fix where the boy is held.
forkB: They know we took their boat on the island today and are setting a watch for us at the tower.
callback: At the Widow's Tooth a little carved horse was left behind. Today, in their boat, a little carved hull was thrown away.
nudge: {friend:Aim}, three willow cuts—one grey, one brown, one white—and tonight a single lamp moving out toward the tower.

puzzle.q: How has Joss been kept on the reed island?
puzzle.clickText: The willow has had fresh shoots cut three days running, and the long shavings in the boat's bilge were carved without haste. They have kept him dry and unharmed on the island by day while moving him across the lake by night.

clicks.text: The willow has had fresh shoots cut three days running, and the long shavings in the boat's bilge were carved without haste. They have kept him dry and unharmed on the island by day while moving him across the lake by night.

fanOutClue.title: Long curls
fanOutClue.text: Every curl in the bottom of the boat is long and unbroken, and all of them are fresh. Nobody hurried him.

narratedSilence: Garrick stands in the doorway looking out into the mist where the water laps at the wall.
questionTitle: A boat lay in the black water right under the tower wall while the map was read aloud. Why was it waiting under an empty tower?
forkA: They posted a listener at the tower waiting for us to assemble the map and speak the way aloud.
forkB: They were keeping watch on the shore road and hid under the wall when they heard our oars.
callback: Yesterday you took their boat. Tonight someone took your words.
nudge: {friend:Aim}, water rings spreading under the stones while our oars were already still, and a brief light out toward the island. Someone was down there before us.

fanOutClue.title: The rings
fanOutClue.text: As you tie up at the tower, rings are already spreading from the dark under its wall, and your oars have been still for a minute.

opener: North, then. That's a long road for tired boots.
questionTitle: The Seekers scattered four Stones to the far corners of the land, yet left the fifth at Highwall. Why keep it in the dead city?
forkA: They kept the fifth at Highwall to stand guard over him where he fell.
forkB: The fifth could not be carried away from Highwall without waking him.
callback: Meira looked for a fifth and never found one. Today, on the road north, somebody had cut a line out of a stone.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, the miles left standing on the stone, and the second line under Highwall cut away to the last letter. Whose name sat under the city's?

puzzle.q: Was the waystone only a road marker, or part of the Seekers' trail?
puzzle.clickText: The line under HIGHWALL was chiselled clean away like the king's face on the coin, and the crack at the stone's foot holds the same unnatural cold as every Seeker housing. The road marker was defaced, and the Seekers set their first sign in its foot.

clicks.text: The line under HIGHWALL was chiselled clean away like the king's face on the coin, and the crack at the stone's foot holds the same unnatural cold as every Seeker housing. The road marker was defaced, and the Seekers set their first sign in its foot.

fanOutClue.title: The crisp edge
fanOutClue.text: Frost has eaten the old carving, but the edges of the cut-out line are crisp. Not one letter of it is left.

opener: The grass on a war grave shouldn't shiver. I'd say that's the heartbeat.
questionTitle: The heartbeat comes from Highwall for a few slow strokes at dusk and dawn, then stops. What is keeping him from waking outright?
forkA: The four Stones have only thinned his sleep; it takes a certain night for him to wake.
forkB: The fifth Stone is still in Highwall, holding the last of the Seekers' lock shut.
callback: On the Stillwater the birds went quiet at the first beat. Tonight the dogs came with it.
nudge: {friend:Might}, one deep bite that held without tearing, and tracks that scattered the moment the beat died. What drove those dogs?

puzzle.q: Were the dogs hunting for themselves?
puzzle.clickText: The dogs came in a straight line from the north while the ground beat, froze mid-stride the instant the beat stopped, and scattered every way after. The beat drove them while it lasted, and let them go when it stopped.

clicks.text: The dogs came in a straight line from the north while the ground beat, froze mid-stride the instant the beat stopped, and scattered every way after. The beat drove them while it lasted, and let them go when it stopped.

fanOutClue.title: Heads down
fanOutClue.text: When the beat stops, every dog stops with it, heads down, mid-stride. Not one runs away, and not one comes on.

opener: High on the wall, and not a breath of green in the whole city. Sit down out of the wind.
questionTitle: Highwall's gate is barred from the inside with fresh timber in brackets worn bright by centuries of bars. Who is keeping it shut?
forkA: The Order — keeping the dead city shut so no outsider disturbs their watch on the hall.
forkB: Wardens left behind on the Seekers' wall — barring the gate to keep what is inside from getting out.
callback: Upriver, somebody kept a hidden path clear and a dog on new iron. Here somebody keeps a new bar on an old gate.
nudge: {friend:Craft}, a broken stair knocked out with hammers long ago, and a fresh timber bar below. Somebody wants only one way in.

puzzle.q: Was the gate barred long ago and left, or is someone tending it now?
puzzle.clickText: The timber bar was felled and squared within the last few days, and a single narrow path is trodden in the dust from the gatehouse straight up toward the smoke. Whoever tends the fire below the hall comes down to bar this gate.

clicks.text: The timber bar was felled and squared within the last few days, and a single narrow path is trodden in the dust from the gatehouse straight up toward the smoke. Whoever tends the fire below the hall comes down to bar this gate.

fanOutClue.title: Go down to it
fanOutClue.text: Stacked against the gatehouse wall lie dozens of old bars, the lowest rotted to a brown line. Whoever changes the bar has kept every one.

narratedSilence: Garrick wipes the dust from the cups with his sleeve, pours one more than there are of you, and sets the last at the empty place by the shuttered window facing up the hill. "Family habit. We always pour one for whoever can't be with us."
questionTitle: Their boots have not stirred the dust in centuries, yet at dusk a helm seemed to turn and metal scraped on stone. Are the standing soldiers waking?
forkA: No — they were frozen where they stood when he fell, and the dusk light played tricks on us.
forkB: Yes — the heartbeat from the hall is beginning to stir them inside their armour.
callback: On the road, when the beat stopped, the dogs stopped where they stood. These soldiers stopped mid-stride, and never started again.
nudge: {friend:Aim}, unbroken dust round every boot, and one sound of iron on stone after we barred the door.

fanOutClue.title: Stop beside one
fanOutClue.text: Its left foot is forward, the heel just lifted. So is the next one's. So is every one's. They all stopped on the same step.

opener: One chalk stroke each dusk. Somebody's counting.
questionTitle: The Order has camped facing the sealed doors for generations, crossing off one stroke each dusk. What are they counting to?
forkA: A fixed night on the calendar that they have known from the beginning.
forkB: A sign from inside the hall as the heartbeat grows strong enough to break the seal.
callback: At Reedham they kept Joss eight nights, waiting for something. Here they strike off one night every dusk.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, every stroke on that board drawn in the same square hand, and every head lifting when the beat comes. What ends when the count ends?

puzzle.q: Is this camp a newly arrived war-band or a permanent post?
puzzle.clickText: The chalk strokes on the board have been gone over in the same hand until the wood is grooved, and extra bedrolls lie rolled and tied around the hearth for men on post. This camp is a permanent watch kept by a regular relief.

clicks.text: The chalk strokes on the board have been gone over in the same hand until the wood is grooved, and extra bedrolls lie rolled and tied around the hearth for men on post. This camp is a permanent watch kept by a regular relief.

fanOutClue.title: One hand
fanOutClue.text: Every stroke on the board is in the same thick, square hand, the crossed ones and the ones still to cross. The chalk has been gone over many times, never redrawn.

opener: A slit window, a hidden room, a night nobody heard you.
questionTitle: The fifth Stone lies inside the wall beneath our feet, and we carry the mark in our blood. What happens when we open that room tonight?
forkA: Our blood will wake the fifth right here in the wall and end his waking.
forkB: Finding the fifth here is only half the task — it will have to be taken to his hall.
callback: Every map before tonight was read out loud. Tonight it went hand to hand, and nobody heard.
nudge: {friend:Aim}, two shallow dips worn into the parapet where elbows rested, facing straight up at the hall.

puzzle.q: How did the room stay hidden from the Order for centuries?
puzzle.clickText: The walkway here was built a full stride wider on the city side, and the slit window is set so low in the stone face that it cannot be seen from the square. Anyone not standing on this parapet would take the wall for solid rock.

clicks.text: The walkway here was built a full stride wider on the city side, and the slit window is set so low in the stone face that it cannot be seen from the square. Anyone not standing on this parapet would take the wall for solid rock.

fanOutClue.title: The narrow slit
fanOutClue.text: The slit is no wider than a hand, low in the wall's face. Unless you lean out over the parapet and look straight down the stone, you cannot see it at all.

place: The wall room, six nights left
opener: Quiet's good in a hole in a wall. I'll take it.
questionTitle: The searchers walked past our door twice and found nothing, yet the watchman at the board still looked down at the wall at dusk. Why?
forkA: He still believes someone is hiding in the wall; the Order has not given up the search.
forkB: He is only checking that the rampart stays dark before he strikes the night's chalk.
callback: At dusk you crossed the wall and nobody heard. By the end of the night a watchman was looking straight at your window.
nudge: {friend:Aim}, he paused with the chalk in his hand and looked down the hill at the wall before he struck the board. Was he hunting a light, or keeping a routine?

puzzle.q: Could a candle inside the niche ever show through the slit?
puzzle.clickText: The stone niche sits deep and low beneath the slit, and its only candle-soot is centuries old. Even when the Seekers kept a light behind the Stone, no flame could ever show in the square.

clicks.text: The stone niche sits deep and low beneath the slit, and its only candle-soot is centuries old. Even when the Seekers kept a light behind the Stone, no flame could ever show in the square.

fanOutClue.title: No light inside
fanOutClue.text: Not a candle burns in the room. Every lantern you can see from the slit is out in the square, and none of them reaches in.

place: The barracks under the wall, five nights left
narratedSilence: Garrick rests his head against the cold masonry, listening to the hollow thud of the earth below in silence.
questionTitle: When the ceiling came down, a hollowed soldier stood in our doorway, looked at the fallen stone, and walked on toward the hall at the heartbeat. What is moving the dead garrison across Highwall?
forkA: The waking heart inside the hall is drawing every soldier back to the place where he fell.
forkB: They are still carrying out their last order from the night the barracks emptied: form ranks at the hall.
callback: Last week you couldn't be sure a helm had turned toward you. Today one stood in your doorway and looked at the fallen stone instead.
nudge: {friend:Agility}, empty spear-racks swept clean, bowls never filled, and every iron boot in the city stepping once when the beat comes.

fanOutClue.title: The swept racks
fanOutClue.text: The spear-racks along the wall are empty, and the dust under every one is swept clean in the same short arc.

place: The great square, four nights left
opener: Warm walls, and more faithful at the gate by the hour. Eat something. It will be a long night.
questionTitle: The hall's stone wall is warm from the floor up behind sealed bronze doors, while new arrivals stack clean robes by their fire outside. Has the Order already set the four Stones inside, or are they still waiting outside for the last night?
forkA: The four Stones are already set around him on the floor inside, warming the stone.
forkB: The Stones are still outside with the faithful, waiting to be carried in on the dark moon.
callback: The soldiers are three streets nearer the hall. Round the Order's fire there are twice as many as before.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, clean robes folded on top of their road-packs outside, and warmth in the stone wall only from knee-height down.

puzzle.q: Where is the heat in the hall's wall coming from?
puzzle.clickText: An unbroken bank of dust lies across the seam of the bronze doors, and the stone wall is warm only from knee-height down. The front doors have never opened, and whatever is warming the hall lies flat on the floor inside.

clicks.text: An unbroken bank of dust lies across the seam of the bronze doors, and the stone wall is warm only from knee-height down. The front doors have never opened, and whatever is warming the hall lies flat on the floor inside.

fanOutClue.title: Eleven watchmen
fanOutClue.text: Eleven watchmen. Six have road-dust to the knee and packs not yet unrolled. They did not send for men to hunt you; these were already coming for the night.

place: The hill behind the hall, three nights left
opener: That hill was steeper than it looked. Sit.
questionTitle: Every other soldier in Highwall faces the hall. Why has this one stood in the mouth of the Seekers' crack since the war ended, facing out?
forkA: The Seekers left it to bar their own secret passage after they sealed the hall and walked out.
forkB: It was keeping the king's last watch — guarding the back of his throne against anyone coming down the hill.
callback: Upriver, a dog on a chain kept the hidden path. Today a soldier stood in the crack with its back to the hall.
nudge: {friend:Craft}, two hollows worn into solid stone by iron boots, and the heartbeat louder right behind the blank rock than anywhere else.

puzzle.q: How long had the sentinel stood in the mouth of the crack?
puzzle.clickText: The grit behind the soldier lay smooth and untouched until your boots marked it, while the rock under its iron soles is worn into two shallow hollows. Nobody has passed down this crack since the war ended, and that soldier never left its post.

clicks.text: The grit behind the soldier lay smooth and untouched until your boots marked it, while the rock under its iron soles is worn into two shallow hollows. Nobody has passed down this crack since the war ended, and that soldier never left its post.

fanOutClue.title: The untouched grit
fanOutClue.text: Past where the soldier stood, the grit on the crack's floor lies smooth and untouched. Your boots are the first marks in it.

opener: Two nights. Eat while there's something to eat.
questionTitle: The sky-watchers' wall stops on the dark moon the night he fell, with a Seeker housing set beside the last cut. Who were the sky-watchers reckoning that cycle for?
forkA: For the Seekers: they marked the cycle so their descendants could count the blank wall and know the hour.
forkB: For the king: they were his own watchers, reckoning the return of the dark moon before the city fell.
callback: The Order's board has counted down for generations. The sky-watchers' wall, counted forward, lands on the same night.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, every row spaced a finger's width apart for generations, and slates on the floor scratched with long sums begun again.

puzzle.q: What were the sky-watchers doing in the days before the wall went blank?
puzzle.clickText: The last rows of moons were chiselled in a rough hurry without missing a single night, while the slates on the floor are covered in long sums crossed through and begun again. They were racing to reckon a distant date before the last night came.

clicks.text: The last rows of moons were chiselled in a rough hurry without missing a single night, while the slates on the floor are covered in long sums crossed through and begun again. They were racing to reckon a distant date before the last night came.

fanOutClue.title: The chisel on the ledge
fanOutClue.text: On the ledge under the last moon, a chisel is lying where it was put down, the mallet beside it. Nobody came back for them.

place: The crack in the hill, one night left
opener: Last night of the count. Eat what you like.
questionTitle: Tomorrow night the Seekers' door opens for our blood, and we carry the fifth Stone into the hall where the four are waiting. What happens when the fifth is brought to him?
forkA: It finishes what the Seekers began — binding him in his sleep before the four Stones can wake him.
forkB: It finishes what the four Stones began — waking him whole, because the fifth is the piece the Order lacked.
callback: Six nights ago you had a hidden room. Tonight you have one stroke left.
nudge: {friend:Intellect}, grit swept in a quarter-circle where the stone door swings inward, and every helm on the hill turned toward the hall.

puzzle.q: Where is the city's garrison tonight?
puzzle.clickText: Every post across the lower streets stands empty now, and every helm on the hill is turned toward the hall. Nothing is left guarding the walls; the entire city is converging on one room.

clicks.text: Every post across the lower streets stands empty now, and every helm on the hill is turned toward the hall. Nothing is left guarding the walls; the entire city is converging on one room.

fanOutClue.title: Every helm to the hall
fanOutClue.text: From the crack's mouth you can see the whole street climbing toward you. Every helm in it is turned to the hall, not one to the hill.
